label: Baire Spaces and Dimension
notes: Open the chapter, which spans printed pages 292 through 316. Two final point-set topics close the first half of the course. The Baire category theorem captures a notion of topological largeness that forbids small sets from filling a space, and dimension theory assigns an integer dimension to spaces and embeds them in Euclidean space.

label: The Baire Category Theorem
notes: A Baire space is one in which a countable union of nowhere dense closed sets has empty interior, equivalently a countable intersection of dense open sets is dense. The Baire category theorem guarantees that complete metric spaces and locally compact Hausdorff spaces are Baire, a result with surprising existence consequences.

label: Applications of Baire
notes: Baire category yields striking existence proofs without explicit construction. The set of continuous nowhere differentiable functions is dense, real numbers are uncountable, and the uniform boundedness principle of functional analysis follows. The method shows that a generic point or function has a property even when no single example is easy to write down.

label: Topological Dimension
notes: The covering dimension assigns to a space the smallest integer such that every open cover has a refinement whose order, the maximum number of overlapping sets, is at most one more than that integer. For nice spaces it matches the intuitive dimension, giving curves dimension one and surfaces dimension two.

label: The Embedding Theorem
notes: A compact metrizable space of covering dimension at most a given integer embeds in Euclidean space of dimension twice that integer plus one. The proof uses general position arguments and the Baire category theorem to perturb maps into embeddings. This bounds how much room a finite-dimensional space needs to sit in Euclidean space.

label: Summary
notes: Baire category supplies a powerful nonconstructive existence tool, while dimension theory makes the intuitive idea of dimension precise and topologically invariant. Together they complete the point-set foundations. We now turn to algebraic topology, where loops and their deformations measure the shape of a space. Next: the fundamental group.
